status_summary: On 2025-02-26 the FTC Chairman created a Joint Labor Task Force to prioritize deceptive, unfair or anticompetitive labor market conduct, listing collusion on DEI metrics among examples of such conduct without mentioning ESG, private equity, prices or output, and on 2026-01-30 the Chairman sent warning letters to 42 law firms in the Mansfield Certification program saying that coordination on DEI-based hiring criteria can violate antitrust law, with no investigation or complaint announced. The FTC also joined DOJ in a 2025-05-22 statement of interest in Texas v. BlackRock, which alleges that asset managers used coal holdings to restrain output, and obtained orders barring advertising agencies from coordinating ad placement on publishers' political or ideological viewpoints: Omnicom and Interpublic (proposed 2025-06-23, finalized in September 2025 with terms that trade press says also cover DEI-commitment criteria), WPP, Publicis and Dentsu (2026-04-15, with eight states) and Havas (2026-06-30), with the court later approving the 2026 orders. A separate FTC demand to Media Matters over the same boycott allegations was blocked by a preliminary injunction, and after the FTC withdrew it the D.C. Circuit dismissed the appeal on 2026-05-04. These actions differ from the chapter in design: the task force is labor-market focused, no ESG or private equity unit was found, and the advertising matters rest on antitrust collusion theories rather than treating refusals of service as an unfair practice.

timeline.event: The FTC Chairman issues a memorandum creating a Joint Labor Task Force of the Bureaus of Competition, Consumer Protection and Economics and the Office of Policy Planning to prioritize investigation of deceptive, unfair or anticompetitive labor market conduct; the memorandum lists collusion or unlawful coordination on DEI metrics among examples of such conduct and does not mention ESG or private equity.

DOJ's Antitrust Division, joined by the FTC, files a statement of interest in Texas v. BlackRock (E.D. Tex.) supporting state attorneys general who allege that BlackRock, State Street and Vanguard used holdings in competing coal producers to induce lower output, and urging denial of the asset managers' motion to dismiss.

FTC announces a proposed consent order in Omnicom's 13.5 billion dollar acquisition of Interpublic that bars coordinating or steering ad spending away from publishers based on political or ideological viewpoints (vote 2-0-1, Commissioner Meador recused); the Federal Register notice follows on 2025-06-26.

FTC approves the final Omnicom and Interpublic order, which trade press reports broadened the restrictions to cover third-party journalistic-standards ratings and DEI commitments as ad-buying criteria (date from the article's publication, which refers to the previous Friday).

D.C. Circuit, 2-1, declines to lift an August 2025 preliminary injunction that bars the FTC from pursuing its civil investigative demand to Media Matters in the advertising-boycott probe; the district court had found the probe likely retaliatory in violation of the First Amendment, and the panel did not rule on the merits.

The FTC Chairman sends warning letters to 42 law firms in the Mansfield Certification program, stating that coordination on DEI-based hiring criteria can violate antitrust law; no investigation or complaint is announced.

Thirteen state attorneys general announce a 29.5 million dollar settlement with Vanguard in the same ESG antitrust suit; claims against BlackRock and State Street continue. The sources do not show the FTC or DOJ as parties to the settlement.

At D.C. Circuit argument in the Media Matters appeal, an FTC lawyer says the agency is negotiating settlements with other targets of its probe into whether advertising and media groups colluded to boycott online platforms.

FTC (vote 1-0-1, Commissioner Meador recused), with eight states, files a complaint in the Northern District of Texas against WPP, Publicis and Dentsu alleging collusion through common brand-safety standards (the release says the conduct violated the antitrust laws without naming the statutes), with proposed orders barring agreements on such standards or ad placement limits based on politically motivated criteria; the FTC page says the court later approved all three orders.

The D.C. Circuit grants the parties' joint stipulation and dismisses the FTC's appeal in Media Matters for America v. FTC (No. 25-5302), after FTC staff withdrew the civil investigative demand on 2026-04-16 and the FTC moved on 2026-04-20 to dismiss the appeal as moot.

title: Create an FTC task force on ESG and DEI collusion and unfair trade practices
uncertainties: The 2025-02-26 task force memorandum, the 2026-01-30 warning-letter release and the 2026-06-30 Havas release were read in this review on ftc.gov; the WPP, Publicis and Dentsu release was read by the researcher. The memorandum lists DEI-metric collusion as an example of labor market conduct within FTC jurisdiction, not as a separate task force responsibility, and contains no ESG, private equity, price-fixing or output terms; whether the task force has taken any ESG-related step is unknown. The FTC releases for the 2026 advertising orders say the conduct violated the antitrust laws without naming the Sherman Act or Section 5, and give no dates for the court approvals. The Texas v. BlackRock statement of interest, the September 2025 Omnicom final order was not re-read; the claim that the final Omnicom order added DEI criteria rests on trade press, and the 2025-06-26 Federal Register notice of the proposed order has no DEI terms. The outcome of the BlackRock motion to dismiss was not found. Private equity enforcement relating to ESG was not found, though FTC private equity cases on other theories exist and were not assessed. An earlier Federal Register search found zero FTC documents mentioning ESG since 2025-01-20. Whether these actions count as ESG or DEI collusion enforcement is a classification judgment: the FTC frames the advertising matters as viewpoint-based boycotts and the task force as a labor-market body.
